_comment: Curated A5 reference material: what the board does, what its circuit blocks are,
the 3900-series diagnostic fault codes, what individual parts are for, and the
places the sources disagree with each other.
Everything here is transcribed or summarised from the 1996 Series II service
manual: §2-222 to §2-228 for the theory, §5-2 for the fault codes, §5-4 for the
procedure, and Figure 7-5 (Ch7 PDF pages 17-20) for the drawing and the three
schematic sheets. Where a statement is this dataset's rather than the manual's,

overview.summary: The output stage of the Wideband AC Module, and the reason a 5700A can source a calibrated sine wave to 30 MHz. It takes a sine wave from one of two places — the Oscillator Output assembly (A13) below 1.1 MHz, or the Wideband Oscillator assembly (A6) above 1.2 MHz — and amplifies it to drive 3.5 V rms into a 50 Ω load at the front panel type N connector. Three things sit around that amplifier and matter as much as it does. A thermal rms sensor (U1) measures the output as a dc voltage, which is what makes the amplitude accurate rather than merely large; a 50 Ω resistive attenuator built from two networks (Z1, Z2) and five relays (K4–K8) reduces it in 10 dB steps from 0 to 70 dB, giving a continuous range of 300 µV to 3.5 V rms; and an overload circuit shunts the sensor and drops out every attenuator relay if the sensor output goes 10% past full scale. Digital control is an 82C55 (U7) driving three relay drivers and a diagnostic multiplexer over the guarded bus. Which of the three operating ranges the board is in decides where the amplitude control comes from: below 12 kHz A12 controls it and A5's loop only protects; from 12 kHz to 1.1 MHz A5's sensor output goes to A11's adc through the RCL line; above 1.2 MHz A5 compares its sensor against DAC OUT and drives A6's amplitude control line directly.
overview.note: A5 is part of Option -03 and is fitted only to instruments that carry the wideband option. On a calibrator without it, the A5 and A6 card slots are empty and Table 6-6 describes a board that is not in the instrument — so if this assembly cannot be found, check the option before suspecting it has been removed. Fault code 3904 is the instrument's own way of saying the same thing. A5 generates no supply of its own: +17 S, S COM and −17 S arrive on P111 19A/19C, 21A/21C and 20A/20C, +5 LH, LH COM and −5 LH on 13A/13C, 15A/15C and 17A/17C, and +5 RLH with RLH COM on 14A/14C and 16A/16C. Six 6-turn chokes (L1–L6) with the tantalums beside them turn each incoming rail into its own S-suffixed net — +17 S becomes +17S, +5 RLH becomes +SRLH — so a fault that looks like one section misbehaving may be one of those six chokes. The board's two coaxial connectors are not interchangeable: J1 is the 1.2–30 MHz input from A6, J2 the output to the front panel.

SENSOR.rails: 10Hz to 32MHz OUTPUT in, RCL and AMPLITUDE CONTROL out
SENSOR.note: The thermal rms sensor and amplitude control loop — the accuracy of the whole module. U1 is the thermal converter: it puts out a dc voltage equal to the rms value of the amplifier output applied to it, available at TP1. U2A integrates that, and U2B with U3 and U12A form a square-root amplifier that keeps the sensor's settling time constant across the range. U5 buffers the result. Below 11 kHz K2A switches C7 in for extra low-frequency filtering. From 12 kHz to 1.1 MHz K10 in the set position sends the buffered output to the RCL line for A11's adc; from 1.2 MHz to 30 MHz U12B compares it against DAC OUT (which K11 makes by tying DAC OUT HI and DAC SENSE HI together) and the difference leaves as the WB AMPLITUDE CONTROL line to A6.

AMP.rails: J1 or 10Hz to 1MHz INPUT in, 10Hz to 32MHz OUTPUT out
AMP.note: The power amplifier, drawn on sheet 2 and outlined on sheet 1. Three stages. The x10 amplifier (Q4–Q10) takes the nominally 700 mV rms signal from A6 through J1 and multiplies it by ten; U11A holds its dc offset near zero. The 10 Hz to 1.1 MHz buffer (Q17, with U11B doing the same offset job) takes the signal from A13 instead. K12 selects between the two and feeds the unity-gain amplifier (Q11–Q16), which raises the power rather than the voltage: it must deliver 3.5 V rms into 50 Ω, so the x10 amplifier has to produce 7.0 V rms because the amplifier's own 50 Ω source impedance — R96, R97, R98 and R99 in parallel with it — halves everything. R41, R42 and C23 divide the output to make OUTPUT OFFSET for the diagnostics.

ATTEN.note: The 50 Ω output attenuator. K4 switches Z1's 10 dB section in or bypasses it, K5 switches its 20 dB section, and K6 and K7 together switch Z2's 40 dB section — 0 to 70 dB in 10 dB steps. K8 is the output relay: energised, it connects the signal to J2 and so to the front panel type N connector. Combined with the amplifier's own continuously variable 10 dB range this gives a 300 µV to 3.5 V rms output. These five are the only non-latching relays on the board, which is why the overload circuit can drop the output simply by disabling their driver.

OVERLOAD.rails: RMS SENSOR DC in, U9 ENABLE out
OVERLOAD.note: The protection circuit, and the one that decides whether the instrument has an output at all. U4A compares the sensor's dc output against a reference set by VR2 (6.4 V compensated zener) and R21. If the sensor reaches 10% past full scale, U4A's output goes negative, U4B turns on FETs Q2 and Q3, and those shunt the sensor's input and output to ground through the 200 Ω resistors R2 and R18, protecting U1. The same negative output turns Q1 off, which takes the U9 ENABLE line high and disables relay driver U9 — dropping out the attenuator relays K4–K7 and the output relay K8 together. Below 12 kHz the same FETs are turned on deliberately, by control line PB0 through U4B, because in that range the sensor is used for overload protection only.

DIGITAL.rails: Guarded digital bus in, relay drives and SDL out
DIGITAL.note: An 82C55 (U7) under software control on the guarded digital bus, generating 24 outputs from three ports. Port A is the common data bus to the three relay drivers. U6 drives the latching relays K1, K2, K10, K11 and K12, enabled by PC3 and strobed by PC2; U9 drives the non-latching attenuator relays K4–K8, strobed by PC0 and enabled by the U9 ENABLE line the overload circuit generates; U10 drives latching relays K3 and K9, strobed by PC1 and enabled by PC3. K9 puts a 50 Ω load (R43 and R44 in parallel) on the RCL line so A11's adc can check the attenuator resistors and relays. U8, a 4051 analog multiplexer selected by PC4–PC6 and enabled by PC7, is the diagnostic path: it puts AMPLITUDE CONTROL, OUTPUT OFFSET, SENSOR CAL or A6's PLL DIAGNOSTIC onto the SDL line for A11's adc to read.

faultCodes.title: A5: 8255 Control Word
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics read back the control word of the 82C55 (U7).
faultCodes.expected: The control word reads back as written
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. U7 is the only device on this board that talks to the CPU, so a control-word failure is U7 itself, its +5 LH supply, or the guarded digital bus arriving on P111.

faultCodes.title: A5: 8255 Port A Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics write data to port A of U7 and read it back.
faultCodes.expected: The data reads back as written
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. Port A is the shared data bus to all three relay drivers (U6, U9, U10), so a stuck bit here shows up as relays that will not change state rather than as a bad reading.

faultCodes.title: A5: 8255 Port B Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics read port B of U7.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. Port B carries WB SP1, WB FBS, the three MUX select lines and WB ON/OFF* out to P111 — including the line that enables A6 — so a fault here can present as a dead Wideband Oscillator.

faultCodes.title: A5: 8255 Port C Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics read port C of U7.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. Port C carries the three relay-driver strobes and enables (PC0–PC3), the multiplexer address (PC4–PC6) and the multiplexer enable (PC7), so a fault here disables either a group of relays or the whole diagnostic path.

faultCodes.title: Optional Assemblies A5/A6 Are Missing
faultCodes.measure: At power-up the instrument checks which assemblies respond. This test verifies that the Wideband Output is not responding.
faultCodes.expected: A5 responds if the -03 wideband option is fitted
faultCodes.verdict: The manual says a failure indicates A5 is probably at fault — but on an instrument that was never built with the wideband option this code is the correct report and not a fault at all. Check that the option is fitted before troubleshooting. Where it is fitted, the code means the board is not answering on the guarded digital bus: U7, its +5 LH supply, or P111 not seated.

faultCodes.title: A5: Rms Sensor At 10MHz
faultCodes.measure: The wideband assemblies are stepped through 3.5 V and 1.2 V at 1.3 MHz, 2.0 V at 3.0 MHz, 1.0 V at 4.1 MHz, 3.3 V at 5.0 MHz and 2.0 V at 6.0, 7.0 and 7.9 MHz. SENSOR CAL, the rms sensor and amplitude control circuit's output, is put on the SDL line by U8 and read by A11's adc.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. This is the sensor loop itself — U1, U2, U3, U5 and U12A — and the multiplexer path that reports it. Check TP1 and TP2 against §5-4 steps 4 and 5 before replacing anything: the same loop is what those steps walk.

faultCodes.title: A5: Rms Sensor At 30MHz
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3907 with the wideband assemblies configured to 3.5 V and 1.2 V at 30.0 MHz.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. Passing 3907 and failing 3908 points at the frequency response of the sensor and the amplifier ahead of it rather than at the loop's dc behaviour — the x10 amplifier stages and their supply decoupling, not U1's dc accuracy.

faultCodes.title: A5: Rms Sensor At 6.5V DC In
faultCodes.measure: The calibrated 6.5 V reference from A11 (BRF6 with its sense line BSRF6) is connected to the rms sensor input. The sensor's nominal 6.5 V output is divided and buffered and read through SENSOR CAL and the SDL line by A11's adc.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. This is the sensor's dc transfer with a known input, so it separates the sensor from everything ahead of it: if 3907 and 3908 fail and this passes, the sensor is good and the amplifier or the attenuators are not. Check that the reference itself is present at TP6 first — it comes from A11.

faultCodes.title: A5/A6: Ampl. Control At 10MHz
faultCodes.measure: The wideband assemblies are set to 3.5 V and then 1.2 V at 1.3 MHz. WB AMPLITUDE CONTROL, the control signal A5 sends to A6, is divided and put on the SDL line for A11's adc.
faultCodes.expected: 4.5 V ±1.0 V at the 3.5 V level, 0.0 V ±0.7 V at the 1.2 V level
faultCodes.verdict: Titled A5/A6 because either can cause it. The line is U12B's output on A5, and what it is servoing is A6's amplitude. A5 is at fault if the level is wrong with the sensor reading correctly (3907 passing); A6 is at fault if the loop is driving hard because the oscillator will not reach amplitude. TP3 is this line.

faultCodes.title: A5/A6: Ampl. Control At 30MHz
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3910 with the wideband assemblies at 3.5 V and 1.2 V at 30.0 MHz.
faultCodes.expected: 4.8 V ±1.0 V at the 3.5 V level, 0.0 V ±0.8 V at the 1.2 V level
faultCodes.verdict: Titled A5/A6 because either can cause it. The 0.3 V difference between this and 3910's 4.5 V is the extra drive A6 needs at the top of the band; a reading that is high here and correct at 10 MHz is an oscillator losing amplitude with frequency rather than a control fault.

faultCodes.title: A5/A6: Output Offset At 10MHz
faultCodes.measure: The wideband assemblies are stepped through the same eight settings as 3907. The unity-gain amplifier's output is measured through the OUTPUT OFFSET line.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. This is a dc measurement on an ac output stage, so it is the offset servos that are suspect — U11A for the x10 amplifier and U11B for the buffer — and the unity-gain stage itself. TP17 reads the same node undivided.

faultCodes.title: A5/A6: Output Offset At 30MHz
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3912 with the wideband assemblies at 3.5 V and 1.2 V at 30.0 MHz.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. Same circuit as 3912; failing only at 30 MHz points at the x10 amplifier path, which is the only stage that is in circuit here and not at low frequency.

faultCodes.title: A5: 0DB Output Attenuation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The 6.5 V reference (BRF6, BSRF6) is connected to the unity-gain amplifier, which drives the output through the attenuators set for 0 dB. The resulting 3.25 V into 50 Ω goes to the RCL line and A11's adc nulls its own dac output against it to find the exact value.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. At 0 dB every attenuator relay is bypassed, so this code tests the reference path (K3A, K3B and K12 in the set position), the unity-gain amplifier and the output relay K8 — not the attenuator networks. If 3914 fails, the higher-attenuation codes will fail with it and mean nothing on their own.

faultCodes.title: A5: 10DB Output Attenuation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3914 with the attenuators set for 10 dB, giving 1.027 V into 50 Ω.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault, and with 3914 passing it is specific: K4 and the 10 dB section of Z1. §5-4 step 9 checks the same thing by hand at 3 V, 1 V, 300 mV and 30 mV.

faultCodes.title: A5: 20DB Output Attenuation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3914 with the attenuators set for 20 dB, giving 0.325 V into 50 Ω.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. With 3914 and 3915 passing, this is K5 and the 20 dB section of Z1. From 20 dB up the Switch Matrix assembly's cal zero amplifier is in the measurement path (§2-228), so a failure at 20 dB and above with 0 and 10 dB good can also be A8.

faultCodes.title: A5: 30DB Output Attenuation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3914 with the attenuators set for 30 dB, giving 0.103 V into 50 Ω.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. 30 dB is K4 and K5 together, so a failure here with 3915 and 3916 both passing is unusual and points at the relays' combination rather than at either section — check the drive from U9 and the contacts, not the networks.

faultCodes.title: A5: 40DB Output Attenuation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The same measurement as 3914 with the attenuators set for 40 dB, giving 0.032 V into 50 Ω.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. 40 dB is the first setting that uses Z2, switched in by K6 and K7 together, so this is the code that separates the second attenuator network from the first.

faultCodes.title: Spare
faultCodes.measure: Not used.
faultCodes.verdict: This fault code is not used.

faultCodes.title: Spare
faultCodes.measure: Not used.
faultCodes.verdict: This fault code is not used.

faultCodes.title: Spare
faultCodes.measure: Not used.
faultCodes.verdict: This fault code is not used.

faultCodes.title: A5/A6: Wideband Initialization Fault
faultCodes.measure: The diagnostics attempt to set the wideband hardware into its test configuration before running any of the measurements above.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. Nothing has been measured yet when this fires, so it is the control path rather than the signal path: U7, the three relay drivers, and the relays failing to latch. Expect the rest of the 3900 series to fail alongside it and to mean nothing until this one is cleared.

faultCodes.title: A5: 8255 Was Reset
faultCodes.measure: The control word of U7 is read back after the diagnostics have run.
faultCodes.expected: The control word is still the one that was written
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A5 is probably at fault. The 82C55 has lost its configuration since it was set — a reset line problem or a supply glitch on +5 LH rather than a dead part, so check the decoupling and the RESET line on P111 before condemning U7.

componentNotes.U1: The thermal rms sensor, and the part the module's ac accuracy rests on. It produces a dc voltage equal to the rms value of the amplifier output applied to it, available at TP1. Ordered as a graded assembly — 'RMS CONVERTER TESTED 400 OHM-B' — not a catalogue part. (§2-225)
componentNotes.U2: Dual precision op amp. U2A is the sensor integrator; U2B is part of the square-root amplifier that keeps the sensor's settling time constant across the range. (§2-225)
componentNotes.U3: Five-transistor NPN array (three isolated, two differentially connected) used with U2B and U12A to form the square-root amplifier. (§2-225)
componentNotes.U4: Dual comparator, and the whole of the overload decision. U4A compares the sensor's dc output against the VR2/R21 reference; U4B drives the gates of Q2 and Q3 and is also what control line PB0 uses to turn them on deliberately below 12 kHz. (§2-226)
componentNotes.U5: Low-offset, low-noise op amp buffering the sensor's dc output. Its output is what K10 puts on the RCL line and what U12B compares against DAC OUT. (§2-225)
componentNotes.U6: Relay driver for the latching relays K1, K2, K10, K11 and K12. Enabled by PC3 of U7 and strobed by PC2, with port A supplying the data. (§2-227)
componentNotes.U7: The 82C55 programmable peripheral interface, and the only device on this board that talks to the CPU. Its 24 outputs are everything: port A is the shared data bus to the three relay drivers, port B carries WB SP1, WB FBS, the multiplexer select lines and WB ON/OFF*, and port C carries the driver strobes and enables and the multiplexer address. (§2-227)
componentNotes.U8: 4051 analog multiplexer, the diagnostic path. PC4–PC6 select between AMPLITUDE CONTROL, OUTPUT OFFSET, SENSOR CAL and A6's WB PLL DIAGNOSTIC; PC7 enables the output onto the SDL line for A11's adc. Three of those four points are on this board and one is on A6. (§2-227)
componentNotes.U9: Relay driver for the non-latching attenuator relays K4–K8. Strobed by PC0 and enabled by the U9 ENABLE line from the overload circuit — which is how an overload drops the output without the software being involved. (§2-226, §2-227)
componentNotes.U10: Relay driver for the latching relays K3 and K9. Strobed by PC1 and enabled by PC3. (§2-227)
componentNotes.U11: Dual op amp doing the same job twice: U11A holds the x10 amplifier's dc output near zero, U11B does it for the 10 Hz to 1.1 MHz buffer. Both are servos rather than signal amplifiers. (§2-223)
componentNotes.U12: Dual op amp. U12A completes the square-root amplifier with U2B and U3; U12B is the amplitude comparator that drives A6 — it compares the buffered sensor output against DAC OUT and sends the difference out as WB AMPLITUDE CONTROL. (§2-225)
componentNotes.Q1: Turned off by U4A's negative output during an overload, which takes the U9 ENABLE line high and disables driver U9 — dropping K4–K7 and the output relay K8. (§2-226)
componentNotes.Q2: One of the two DMOS FETs that shunt the rms sensor's input to ground through R2 during an overload, and deliberately below 12 kHz. (§2-222, §2-226)
componentNotes.Q3: The second shunt FET, on the sensor's output through R18. §5-4 steps 4 and 5 check both by reading TP5 rather than the FETs themselves. (§2-222, §2-226)
componentNotes.Q17: The 10 Hz to 1.1 MHz buffer. Everything below 1.1 MHz arrives from A13 and passes through this one JFET before reaching K12 and the unity-gain amplifier. (§2-223)
componentNotes.Q18: The DMOS power FET that returns the latching relay coils. §5-4 does not mention it, but sheet 3's own note does: 'FET Q18 is on for all functions except attenuator calibration'.
componentNotes.K1: Input select. In the set position it takes the signal from A13 for 10 Hz to 1 MHz operation; K1 and K12 are driven from the same lines and move together. (§2-227)
componentNotes.K3: Switches the 6.5 V reference (BRF6) into the unity-gain amplifier for attenuator calibration, with K12. Latching, driven by U10. (§2-228)
componentNotes.K8: The output relay. Energised, it connects the attenuator output to J2 and so to the front panel; de-energised — including by an overload — there is no output at all. (§2-224, §2-226)
componentNotes.K9: Puts a 50 Ω load (R43 and R44 in parallel) on the RCL line so A11's adc can measure the output and check the attenuator resistors and relays. Sheet 3 notes that K9 is used during instrument diagnostics. (§2-227)
componentNotes.K10: In the set position, connects the sensor and amplitude control output to the RCL line for A11's adc — the 12 kHz to 1.1 MHz control path. (§2-222, §2-225)
componentNotes.K11: Ties DAC OUT HI and DAC SENSE HI together to create DAC OUT, the amplitude demand U12B servos to above 1.2 MHz. (§2-222, §2-225)
componentNotes.K12: Selects which amplifier drives the unity-gain stage: reset for the x10 amplifier (1.2–30 MHz), set for the 10 Hz to 1.1 MHz buffer. Driven from the same lines as K1. (§2-223, §2-227)
componentNotes.Z1: Thick-film attenuator network carrying the 10 dB and 20 dB sections, switched by K4 and K5. Marked as a static-sensitive part in both parts lists. (§2-224)
componentNotes.Z2: Thick-film attenuator network carrying the 40 dB section, switched by K6 and K7 together. (§2-224)
componentNotes.VR2: The 6.4 V compensated, 2 ppm reference zener that sets the overload threshold with R21. It is the only precision zener on the board and §5-4 step 8 is the test of it. (§2-226)
componentNotes.R2: One of the two 200 Ω resistors through which Q2 and Q3 shunt the rms sensor. (§2-226)
componentNotes.R18: The second 200 Ω sensor shunt resistor, on the sensor's output side. (§2-226)
componentNotes.R41: With R42 and C23, divides the amplifier output by ten to create the OUTPUT OFFSET signal the diagnostics read through U8. Not the same node as TP17, which taps the output undivided through R115. (§2-223)
componentNotes.R43: With R44 in parallel, the 50 Ω load K9 puts on the RCL line for the attenuator diagnostic. Both are 100 Ω 0.1% parts. (§2-227)
componentNotes.R44: With R43 in parallel, the 50 Ω load K9 puts on the RCL line. (§2-227)
componentNotes.R96: One of the four 187 Ω 0.1% resistors that, in parallel with the unity-gain amplifier's own output resistance, form the 50 Ω output impedance. Their tolerance is the output level's tolerance. (§2-223)
componentNotes.R97: One of the four 187 Ω 0.1% output resistors. (§2-223)
componentNotes.R98: One of the four 187 Ω 0.1% output resistors. (§2-223)
componentNotes.R99: One of the four 187 Ω 0.1% output resistors. (§2-223)
componentNotes.C7: Switched into the rms sensor circuit by K2A in the 10 Hz to 11 kHz range to add filtering for low-frequency signals. (§2-225)
componentNotes.C26: The 4.7 µF tantalum on +SRLH beside the attenuator relay coils on sheet 3 — the local reservoir for the non-latching relays K4–K8, which are the only coils on this board that hold current continuously.
componentNotes.C82: The board's only aluminium electrolytic: 47 µF on +SLH at the 82C55 and the relay drivers (sheet 3, zone D5). Everything else on this board that is not ceramic or polyester is a solid tantalum.
componentNotes.E3: The link across J3 that closes the amplitude control loop between DAC OUT and TP18. §5-4 steps 6 and 8 both begin by removing it and end by telling you to put it back; left off, the board cannot regulate its output.
componentNotes.J1: The right-angle SMB coaxial connector carrying the 1.2 MHz to 30 MHz sine wave in from the Wideband Oscillator assembly (A6) over a 75 Ω cable. §5-4 step 7 names the cable at this connector as the first thing to suspect when the x10 amplifier input looks wrong. (§2-222)
componentNotes.J2: The right-angle SMB coaxial connector carrying the attenuator output to the front panel WIDEBAND type N connector, through K8. (§2-224)
componentNotes.W1: The wideband output interconnect cable, drawn on the locator between J2 and the front panel and printed across the middle of the board.
componentNotes.MP1: The 50 Ω N-type termination supplied with the option. §5-4 step 1 requires it on the front panel connector before any measurement in the section is meaningful, and step 9 measures across it.
componentNotes.W2: The 3 ft 50 Ω N-type output cable supplied with the option. §5-4 step 9 uses it for the final end-of-cable check after wideband gain calibration.
componentNotes.CP1: BNC(F) to banana plug(M) adapter, supplied with the wideband option. Not a part of the board — it has no silkscreen designator and no position on the drawing.
componentNotes.CP2: BNC(M) to N(F) coaxial adapter, supplied with the wideband option. Not a part of the board.
componentNotes.CP3: The test lead pouch the wideband accessories are kept in. Listed in Table 6-6 but absent from the Rev 9 list, and not a part of the board.

caveats.title: This board is only in the instrument if the wideband option is
caveats.text: A5 and A6 are Option -03, the Wideband AC Module. A 5700A or 5720A built without it has empty A5 and A6 slots, no type N connector on the front panel, and no board matching Figure 7-5 anywhere inside — the chassis is otherwise identical, which is what makes this worth saying. The instrument reports the same thing itself as fault code 3904, 'Optional Assemblies A5/A6 Are Missing', and on an unequipped calibrator that code is correct rather than a fault. Both the locator caption and Table 6-6 carry '(Option -03)' in their titles.

caveats.title: R123–R128: four sources, three different answers
caveats.text: Table 6-6 in the 1996 manual has no R123–R128 at all. Instead its choke row reads 'L1-6,L18,L123-128  CHOKE,6TURN' against a Tot Qty of 7 — thirteen designators for seven parts — and carries footnote 1, 'L123, L124- alternate PN 452888 if there is difficulty meeting 30 MHz specificaiton'. The Rev 9 list prints the same choke row as 'L 1- 6, 18' for the same Tot Qty of 7, with no L123-128, and lists 'R 123-128  RES,CF,10,+-5%,0.25W' stock 807669 as its own row against a Tot Qty of 6. Schematic sheet 3 draws six 10 Ω resistors, hand-lettered R123 to R128, one in series with each of the K5–K8, K3 and K9 coil returns. The board silkscreens R123–R128. And the photographed board has 6-turn ferrite chokes (Midcom 40699) fitted at those pads, not resistors. This dataset follows Rev 9 and the drawing: the six are carried as R123–R128, 10 Ω carbon film, and the phantom L123–L128 is removed so the choke row's own quantity matches. If your board has chokes there, it is not wrong — the footnote says the position takes one.

caveats.title: Three of Table 6-6's quantities do not match their own designator lists
caveats.text: Four rows in the 1996 table count wrong, and the Rev 9 list settles three of them. 'Q11-13' and 'Q14-16' each list three designators against a Tot Qty of 2; Rev 9 gives Q11–Q13 as three MRF545s and Q9, Q10, Q14, Q15 and Q16 as five MRF544s, and sheet 2 prints those eight device types beside those eight transistors, so the designator lists are right and the quantities are wrong. The 0.1 µF polyester row lists 35 designators against a Tot Qty of 36; Rev 9's equivalent row lists 33 (it has no C30 or C31) against a Tot Qty of 33, so the 1996 row's count is one too many and no 36th designator exists — C24 and C54 are the only unused capacitor numbers on this board and neither is printed on the drawing. The fourth, 'H7-9' against a Tot Qty of 4, both revisions print identically and neither resolves; three screws are listed and four are counted.

caveats.title: Eleven parts changed stock number between the two revisions
caveats.text: Joining the two parts lists on Fluke stock number leaves eleven rows that do not join, and every one is a genuine re-sourcing rather than a scan error. Most are resistors of identical value and tolerance bought from a different vendor: R41, R47, R48/R49/R51/R55/R61/R65/R71/R76/R77/R84/R85/R90/R91, R50, R52, R53, R66, R74, R75, R100 and R115. Three matter more. Q9, Q10 and Q14–Q16 are ST1020 (stock 1590835) in the 1996 list and MRF544 (912522) in Rev 9, and Q11–Q13 are ST2525A (1575948) against MRF545 (866769) — schematic sheet 2 prints MRF544 and MRF545, so the drawing agrees with the as-built part rather than with the later list. U1, the thermal rms converter, is 842591 in the 1996 list and 767707 in Rev 9; the photographed board's U1 is marked with both numbers. H7–H9 changed from a stainless lock screw to a plain steel machine screw. In every case the app shows the 1996 part in the main fields and the Rev 9 part as 'as built'.

caveats.title: U2 and U12: the schematic agrees with neither parts list about the device
caveats.text: Rev 9 lists U2, U11 and U12 on one row as LF412ACN (stock 851704). The 1996 list keeps U11 there and moves U2 and U12 to stock 783696, 'IC,OP AMP,DUAL,PRECISION,8-PIN'. Schematic sheets 1 and 2 print 'LT1013' beside U2A, U2B, U11A, U11B, U12A and U12B — all three. The LT1013 and the LF412 are not interchangeable in every respect: one is a precision bipolar dual, the other a JFET-input dual an order of magnitude faster. U2 and U12 are in the sensor and amplitude control loop where offset matters, and U11 is a pair of dc servos in the amplifier where speed does. The dataset carries the 1996 part in the main fields and the Rev 9 part as 'as built'; check what is actually fitted before ordering.

caveats.title: C32 is in one parts list and on no schematic sheet
caveats.text: Table 6-6's first tantalum row is 'C16,C18,C26,C39-44,C32' for a Tot Qty of 10, and the ten designators match. Rev 9's equivalent row is 'C 16- 18, 21, C 26, 39- 44' for a Tot Qty of 11 — the same parts plus C17 and C21, which the 1996 list splits into a second row, but without C32. None of the three schematic sheets draws a C32. So C32 exists only in the 1996 revision of the parts list; it is carried here with that list's description, and it may not be placeable on the drawing.

caveats.title: The Note between steps 4 and 5 names two test points on a different board
caveats.text: §5-4's Note before step 5 says that if the instrument trips to standby while you are probing, 'defeat the monitoring by connecting a jumper from TP9 to TP10 on the DAC assembly'. A5 has its own TP9 and TP10 — 10Hz-1MHz INPUT and X10 AMP BIAS 1 — and jumpering those two would tie the buffer input to the x10 amplifier's bias network. The two references are suppressed from step 4's links for that reason; the sentence still says what to do, and the assembly it says to do it on is A11.

caveats.title: Figures 5-1 to 5-5 belong to A6, not to this section
caveats.text: The five waveform plates printed on manual pages 5-42 to 5-46 sit inside and just after §5-4's page range, and Figure 5-1 begins on the same page §5-4 ends on. None of them is cited by §5-4, which makes no oscilloscope-waveform comparison at all — its one scope measurement, step 7, asks only for a distortion-free sine wave and a ten-times ratio. All five are cited by §5-5, the Wideband Oscillator (A6) section: Figure 5-1 by step 2 (TP10), 5-2 by step 3 (TP1), 5-3 by step 4 (TP15), and 5-4 and 5-5 by the steps after those. The test points they name are A6's, not A5's.

caveats.title: §5-5's opening sentence calls A6 'the Wideband Oscillator assembly (A5)'
caveats.text: The section that follows this board's, §5-5 Troubleshooting the Wideband Oscillator Assembly (A6), opens 'Proceed as follows to troubleshoot the Wideband Oscillator assembly (A5):'. It is a typo — the heading, the steps and the figures are all A6's — but it is worth knowing about, because searching the text layer for 'A5' finds it and it reads like a cross-reference to this board.

caveats.title: The revision on the board, in the manual, and in the etch are three different numbers
caveats.text: The locator drawing and the photographed board both silkscreen '761346 REV' with the letter field left blank and stamped per board, as on A11, A19, A8 and A9. On this board it was never stamped: someone has hand-marked 'REV 104' in marker beside it instead, which is what the dataset records. Table 6-1's Manual Status Information gives this assembly revision level 105, so the board in the photograph is one level behind the manual. Under the silkscreen the etch legend reads '5700A-3011 REV F', which is the artwork revision and a third numbering again. The board also carries a '923' date stamp — 1992, week 23.

caveats.title: The pale rectangle at the left is board, not a shield
caveats.text: This dataset used to say that the attenuator shields were still fitted over the K4-K9 section, that nothing left of about x=0.28 was visible, and that the photograph therefore could not be registered to the drawing. All three were wrong, and the mistake is worth recording because it is easy to repeat: the large pale rectangle in the left third of the photograph looks exactly like a sheet-metal lid, and it is not one. It is the PTFE RF laminate the attenuator is built on — part of the board, bonded into it, with a ring of plated ground vias round its edge, its own through-hole pads with solder fillets, and its own yellow silkscreen. Z1, Z2, K4 to K9, C25-C37, R43 and R44 are all printed on it and all readable, and the K4-K8 relay cans, both SIP attenuator networks and K9's Aromat relay sit on it in plain view. The blue PCB runs round all four sides of it. None of the four sheet-metal shields — M2 rear output, M3 wideband amp front, M4 and M5 attenuator — is fitted on the photographed board, so nothing on the component side is hidden by one. The photograph is now registered to the drawing from 32 landmark pairs, four of them on the laminate itself, and Photo, Overlay and Swipe work.

caveats.title: TP17 and the OUTPUT OFFSET net are not the same node
caveats.text: The sheet 1 legend names TP17 'OUTPUT OFFSET', and §2-223 says OUTPUT OFFSET is what R41, R42 and C23 create. They are not the same point. TP17 taps the amplifier output through R115 (200 kΩ) with C81 (0.47 µF) to SCOM — a filter with unity dc gain, at sheet 2 zone D1. The OUTPUT OFFSET signal that reaches U8's multiplexer input on sheet 3 is the same node divided by R41/R42 (180 kΩ / 20 kΩ) at sheet 2 zone C1, a tenth of it. Fault codes 3912 and 3913 state their 20 mV limit for 'the output of the Unity Gain Amplifier circuit', so it applies at TP17 as printed and to a tenth of that at the multiplexer.
